title: test-0039-MAT-BASICGEOM
passage: Rohan and Meera were drawing a map for their school project. Rohan drew a triangle with its base tilted sideways. Meera asked, 'Is that still a triangle?' Rohan nodded, explaining that a triangle is a closed figure with three straight sides, regardless of its orientation. Next, they needed to mark a path. Meera drew a line segment from point A to point B. She noted that segment AB is identical to segment BA because the distance between the two points remains the same. To represent the school gate, they drew a ray starting from the gate and extending infinitely. Rohan reminded her that a ray can point in any direction, not just to the right. Finally, they drew a circle to mark the playground. Meera drew a line connecting two points on the circle, but it did not pass through the centre. Rohan corrected her, saying that a diameter must pass through the centre of the circle to be valid. They realized that geometry is about precise definitions, not just how shapes look or which way they point. By following these rules, their map was accurate and ready for the class presentation.
